summary: Five microhistorical and intellectual-history practitioners gain individual entries: Ginzburg, Levi, Skinner, Pocock and Koselleck. Existing IDs and bounded source qualifications are retained. Twelve explicitly person-specific edge endpoints are repaired in place; collective field claims remain. New primary readings add the 1996 Pocock–Koselleck exchange, Pocock’s specific Skinner objection, Levi’s qualified 2019 global-history intervention and Skinner’s 1998 publication context.
authorization: User, 2026-10-24: address Gemini coverage feedback before returning to other work, explicitly authorizing sub-agents to split the work. Coordinator assigned this five-person microhistory/intellectual-history batch. No publication authorized.
rationale: Each existing roster identity is promoted without an identity merge. Every new person has at least two substantive incident relationships and three dated contributions backed by the retained/fresh own-text reading or an explicitly named substantive reader. Existing person-specific claims move with their IDs rather than being cloned; aggregate field-to-field claims naming multiple historians remain. New edges distinguish individual contributions, limited objections and a non-directional comparison. Date, publication, translation, symposium and reception are explicit, with no continuous career or review-through year.

The 1969 article pp. 37–38 supplies contemporary explicit question/answer reception; pp. 50–51 also criticize a particular Collingwood inference, recorded as a separate critique.
